messages.subject: untraceable error
parts:
Hello

Would anyone help me figure out why I am getting a generic error when I try running the model below. The model runs well without the spatial component f(id,....

I am attaching the graph file and the data set. 

g<-inla.read.graph("zones.graph")
formula=response~cov1 + cov1sq+ cov2 + cov1:cov2 + cov1sq:cov2 + f(id, model="bym", graph=g,adjust.for.con.comp = FALSE)
mod = inla(formula, data=data,family="poisson", verbose=TRUE, control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=0.1), control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), E=(weight)) 

Here is the error:
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does help; please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Any help to solve the problem will be deeply appreciated.

Thanks,

Victor.

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] untraceable error
parts:
On Wed, 2016-03-02 at 13:03 -0800, Víctor Hugo Gutiérrez Vélez wrote:
> Hello
>
> Would anyone help me figure out why I am getting a generic error when
> I try running the model below. The model runs well without the
> spatial component f(id,....
>
> I am attaching the graph file and the data set.

Hi, 

its a large model and it use quite some memory. (I tried it here). I
guess you run out of MEM and the program stop (in some external
library). 

to reduce memory requirement, try to remove dic/cpo calculations
(mainly cpu), set control.inla = list(int.strategy="eb",
strategy="gaussian"))

you may need to reduce the number of threads used, like adding
num.threads=1 or 2. 

and see how it goes. 

if you does not succeed, we may have a larger machine here you can run
on. 

H
